title: The AI comeback: big data, GPUs and deep learning
summary: What changed after the winters, the three ingredients of the comeback with their pioneers, AlexNet's breakthrough, and the deck's conclusion.

chunks.heading: What changed after the winters
chunks.explanation_md:
AI did not stay frozen.
- **Late 1990s to 2000s**: the rise of **faster processors, larger datasets and neural networks** rebooted AI research.
- **2012+**: **deep learning breakthroughs** (e.g. **AlexNet**) marked **AI's full comeback**.

The deck's picture sums up the formula: **The AI Comeback = Big Data + GPUs + Deep Learning**, on a timeline from **2000 to 2012**:
- **Big Data**: Google, Facebook, Amazon generate massive amounts of user data.
- **GPUs**: in **2006**, **NVIDIA launches CUDA** for general-purpose GPU computing.
- **Deep Learning**: in **2012**, **AlexNet** achieves breakthrough results in image classification.
chunks.exam_line: AI came back through Big Data + GPUs + Deep Learning; deep learning breakthroughs such as AlexNet (2012) marked the full comeback.

chunks.heading: Big Data: the fuel
chunks.explanation_md:
**Key enablers:** **Google, Facebook, Amazon, Baidu, Microsoft**. These tech giants began collecting **massive user behavior, image, text and speech data in the 2000s**.

**Notable events and figures:**
- Google's **Jeff Dean & Sanjay Ghemawat** built **MapReduce** and the **Google File System** to process massive datasets.
- **Amazon Web Services (AWS)** made **storage and distributed computing affordable** for startups and researchers.

**Impact:** it became possible to **train AI models on millions or billions of examples**, so deep learning could **generalize well**.

chunks.heading: GPUs: the powerhouse
chunks.explanation_md:
**Key innovators:**
- **NVIDIA**, particularly **Ian Buck**, developer of **CUDA (2006)**.
- **Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Geoffrey Hinton**, who used GPUs for deep learning in **AlexNet (2012)**.

**Game-changer:** **CUDA (Compute Unified Device Architecture)** let researchers write **general-purpose programs on GPUs**. GPUs turned out to be **100x faster than CPUs** for training deep neural networks.

**Impact:** training that used to take **weeks with CPUs** could now be done in **days or hours**, enabling rapid experimentation and breakthroughs in vision, NLP and speech.

chunks.heading: Deep learning: the brain
chunks.explanation_md:
**Key figures**, known as the **"Godfathers of Deep Learning"**, who won the **Turing Award in 2018**:
- **Geoffrey Hinton** (University of Toronto): **Father of Deep Learning**.
- **Yann LeCun** (Facebook AI): creator of **Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)**.
- **Yoshua Bengio** (Montreal): advanced **sequence models and optimization**.

**Breakthrough moment: AlexNet (2012)** won the **ImageNet competition** with **85% accuracy, 10% better than anyone before**. It used **deep CNNs + ReLU activation + dropout + two GPUs**.

**Impact:** sparked massive interest in neural networks and led to an explosion of **AI startups**, **AI labs (Google Brain, DeepMind, OpenAI)** and real-world products.

chunks.heading: The synergy, and the conclusion
chunks.explanation_md:
No single piece did it alone. The deck's **synergy table**:

| Component | Pioneer(s) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Big Data | Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat (Google) | Gave AI the **raw material to learn** |
| GPUs | Ian Buck (NVIDIA), Krizhevsky | Made AI training **fast and scalable** |
| Deep Learning | Hinton, LeCun, Bengio | Created models that could **learn deeply from data** |

**Conclusion:** AI didn't come back by accident. It returned because of:
- **massive data availability** (thanks to the web),
- **affordable compute power** (via GPUs),
- **powerful algorithms** (deep neural networks).

This **AI Renaissance, launched around 2012**, laid the foundation for **GPT, DALL·E, AlphaFold, ChatGPT** and many more.

questions.model_answer_md:
After the AI winters, AI returned through three forces working together. The deck sums it up as **The AI Comeback = Big Data + GPUs + Deep Learning**, on a timeline from **2000 to 2012**.

**1. Big Data: the fuel**
- **Google, Facebook, Amazon, Baidu, Microsoft** collected massive user behavior, image, text and speech data in the 2000s.
- **Jeff Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat** (Google) built **MapReduce** and the **Google File System**; **AWS** made storage and distributed computing affordable.
- **Impact:** models could train on **millions or billions of examples**.

**2. GPUs: the powerhouse**
- **Ian Buck** at **NVIDIA** developed **CUDA (2006)**, letting researchers write general-purpose programs on GPUs.
- GPUs were **100x faster than CPUs** for training deep networks; **weeks became days or hours**.

**3. Deep Learning: the brain**
- **Geoffrey Hinton** (Father of Deep Learning), **Yann LeCun** (creator of **CNNs**) and **Yoshua Bengio** (sequence models and optimization), the **Godfathers of Deep Learning**, won the **Turing Award in 2018**.
- **AlexNet (2012)** won **ImageNet** with **85% accuracy, 10% better than anyone before**, using deep CNNs, ReLU, dropout and two GPUs.

**The synergy table**

| Component | Pioneer(s) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Big Data | Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat (Google) | Gave AI the **raw material to learn** |
| GPUs | Ian Buck (NVIDIA), Krizhevsky | Made AI training **fast and scalable** |
| Deep Learning | Hinton, LeCun, Bengio | Models that **learn deeply from data** |

AlexNet shows the synergy best: the deck's diagram links both big data and GPUs to AlexNet (2012), which used deep CNNs.

**Conclusion:** no single piece did it alone; data, compute and algorithms together brought AI back.

questions.stem: AI didn't come back by accident. Explain what changed after the AI winters and why around 2012 is called the start of an AI Renaissance.
questions.model_answer_md:
The deck's conclusion says **AI didn't come back by accident**. Specific changes ended the winters.

**What changed after the winters**
- **Late 1990s to 2000s:** the rise of **faster processors, larger datasets and neural networks** rebooted AI research.
- **2012+:** **deep learning breakthroughs** such as **AlexNet** marked **AI's full comeback**.

**The three reasons AI returned**
1. **Massive data availability**, thanks to the web.
2. **Affordable compute power**, via **GPUs** (NVIDIA launched **CUDA in 2006**).
3. **Powerful algorithms**: **deep neural networks**.

**Why 2012 is the turning point**
- In **2012**, **AlexNet** achieved breakthrough results in image classification, winning **ImageNet** with **85% accuracy, 10% better than anyone before**.
- It **sparked massive interest** in neural networks and an explosion of **AI startups** and **AI labs (Google Brain, DeepMind, OpenAI)**.
- The deck calls this the **AI Renaissance, launched around 2012**.

**What it led to**
- It laid the foundation for **GPT, DALL·E, AlphaFold, ChatGPT** and many more.

**Conclusion:** data from the web, cheap GPU compute and deep neural networks came together around 2012, which is why the comeback was planned progress, not luck.
